【原视频简介】
Three local AI models. Five rounds of testing. And one surprisingly difficult question: which model should actually be your daily driver?

I put Quen 3.6 27B, Nematron 3.5 Lightning, and Muse Glimmer through a structured comparison based on the tasks I actually care about—not synthetic leaderboard scores.

We test reasoning, instruction-following, long-context retrieval, resistance to confident pushback, structured extraction, and real agentic tool use. And along the way, two bugs in my own benchmark nearly caused me to publish completely wrong results.

The biggest surprise wasn't a benchmark number.

It was a brown bear.

What I tested

• 13 modified trick questions across all three models
• Harder traps designed to expose memorized-answer behavior
• The modified Monty Hall problem
• The famous brown bear riddle
• What happens when you confidently tell a model that its correct answer is wrong
• Long-context retrieval at 10K, 40K, 80K, and 120K tokens
• Prefill speed and sustained retrieval accuracy
• Real agentic workflows with executable tools
• Multi-step shipment penalty calculations
• Inventory aggregation and purchase-order decisions
• Structured data extraction and date handling

All three models were tested at Q4 quantization, with the same sampling settings, temperature zero, fixed seed, and fully resident on GPU.
